title: Lighthouse, WebPageTest and the browser performance panel

videos.script:
A number tells you that a page is slow. A tool has to tell you why. {{tools}} This lesson uses three: Lighthouse, which loads a page and grades it; the browser's performance panel, which shows what the main thread did, millisecond by millisecond; and WebPageTest, which loads it from somewhere else in the world.

{{score}} You will run Lighthouse against the planner and read how it reaches its score: five metrics, a weight for each, and a phone it pretends to be. {{heavy}} Then a catalogue of five thousand courses, a score of seventy-five, and a report that names the cause. One change on the server, and the score is a hundred.

{{model}} On the way you will catch Lighthouse's model disagreeing with a real slow network by three seconds, and find out which of the two was right.

{{trace}} Then a trace of the main thread, the same file the performance panel opens, read by a small program of your own. {{waterfall}} And a waterfall, which shows the one thing every slow page has in common: requests that wait for each other.
